# Preface
## to the Lover of these Noble Writings.

The God-loving reader <note>A traditional 17th-century greeting to the pious reader.</note> receives herewith a triple index for all the theosophical <term>theosophical: Referring to "Divine Wisdom," a branch of mystical philosophy seeking direct knowledge of the nature of God and the created world.</term> writings of the blessed and highly-enlightened Jacob Böhme <note>Jacob Böhme (1575–1624) was a German mystic and master shoemaker whose visionary writings on the nature of God, light, and darkness deeply influenced Western philosophy and Christian mysticism.</note>; these have not only been diligently revised and improved for this new edition, but have also, through God’s goodness, been augmented with many beautiful additions. And since this work—given its manifold usefulness—cannot be anything but pleasant and joyful to the reader, we have likewise felt encouraged to provide him with sufficient information regarding the arrangement of these indexes and everything else that might be noteworthy therein.

2. The first index is a **VOCABULARY**, or a thorough explanation of all Magic-Mystical <term>Terms</term> <note>original: "Terminorum," the Latin plural for "terms."</note> which the author uses in his writings, especially according to the meaning of the Spirit; additionally, other occurring Latin words have not been omitted, for the sake of those who are not familiar with that language. Regarding the first kind, God has [given] the reader an incompar- <note>The word is cut off by the page break; the catchword "ver-" suggests "unvergleichliche" or "incomparable."</note>

All these newly entered passages are marked with an asterisk (*), as a notice to the God-loving reader; and just as love was born in *Sophia* <note>Divine Wisdom</note> through this work, bringing the Spirit of Christ into it so that readers might be turned from the letter to the soul <note>original: "Gemüth," referring to the inner mind, disposition, or heart.</note> and lifted out of darkness into the light: so She <note>Wisdom/Sophia</note> has given herself to those souls who hunger for God, to unlock their hearts, that they may be awakened to the joy and praise of God. Furthermore, great care has been taken to explain all other words more clearly and correctly wherever it was necessary.

The third is an index of all the **Theosophical Subject Matters** <note>These are the core spiritual and philosophical topics explored by Böhme, such as the nature of the Divine or the origin of the soul.</note> treated by the author, as well as the most remarkable words and names occurring therein; where the reader may look up every matter under its respective letter and find the entire treatise on the same (as it is to be found in the <term>treatises</term> <note>original: "Tractaten"</note> and their chapters and paragraphs indicated alongside) concentrated, or presented in a clear brevity. This is intended for the significant easing of comprehension and the kindling of knowledge in these high and deep matters, to the heartfelt praise of **GOD**. This index has been thoroughly revised in the best possible way for this new edition; efforts have been made to put everything in its right place and to arrange it in better order. Superfluous or doubly-cited entries have been omitted, and the subject matters—where it could be done without detriment to clarity—have been expressed more concisely. Any encountered <term>errata</term> or <term>printing errors</term> <note>original: "Druck-Fehler"</note>, as well as whatever else was necessary to change, have been diligently improved. The reader will find this to be true upon <term>comparison</term> <note>original: "Conferirung"</note> of this new edition with the edition of the year 1715. Nevertheless, the general arrangement of the index has been maintained for internal reasons <note>original: "gemüthlichen Ursachen," referring to the spiritual or conceptual logic behind the original structure.</note>, though we have chosen to divide the realities occurring under each title into their own distinct paragraphs for greater clarity.

-># Preface.<-

5. Furthermore, in this current new edition, this **Subject Index**—no less than the first one, or the so-called **Vocabulary**—has been adorned with a beautiful and lovely little pearl. God has so ordained it that we are able to share with the reader, for their blessing, several extraordinary notes by the late and dearly proven **practitioner of faith** <note>original: "Glaubens-Practici," referring to one who lives out their spiritual convictions through experience rather than just theory</note> regarding these noble spiritual writings: Mr. Johann Georg Gichtel <note>Gichtel (1638–1710) was a famous German mystic and a primary editor/promoter of Jacob Böhme's works; his annotations were highly prized by followers.</note>. These are notes he recorded long ago while reading these works. Those who are connoisseurs, or even just souls who long for God, will find therein the core of the **Theosophical Matters** handled by the author, full of the sweetness and power of the Spirit. Through this, they will be awakened to the praise of God and to gratitude for this unexpected gift of grace in the love of Jesus. These notes have been inserted throughout in their proper places and marked with a preceding asterisk (*), as a pleasant notice for the enthusiast.

6. Moreover, the writings of the author have been listed in the indexes in the very same order as they appear in the work itself, though they have been abbreviated (according to the instructions following hereafter). Where numbers previously appeared alongside a treatise title, these have been omitted to prevent any confusion with the subsequent numbers of chapters and paragraphs. Therefore, one has used, for example <note>original: "z. e." for "zum Exempel"</note>, **Questions on the Soul**, or **Soul-Qu.**, instead of *40 Questions on the Soul*; likewise <note>original: "it." for "item"</note> **Theosophical Points** for *6 Theosophical Points*; furthermore **Mystic Points** for *6 Mystic Points*; and finally **Theosophical Questions** for *177 Theosophical Questions*. Great care has been taken to print the numbers themselves cleanly, clearly, and accurately; and finally, in a

7. Finally, in the indexes of this new edition, when citing the treatises, instead of the page and section numbers used in the 1715 edition <note>original: "Edit. von Ao. 1715," refers to the previous collected edition of Böhme's works</note>, only the chapters and paragraphs <note>The symbol § is used for paragraphs</note> or sections of each place have been introduced with great diligence. Thus, the first number indicates the chapter and the second the paragraph or section. Consequently, these mentioned indexes—and especially the third one, the **Subject Index** <note>original: "Realien," referring to a "Real Index," which indexes concepts and topics rather than just words or names</note>—can also be used with great benefit for the previous editions, particularly the one from 1682. May the love of God in Christ Jesus grant this to every God-seeking reader for the eternal joy of the spirit!

## The First Index.
# VOCABULARY
->or<-
### Explanation
->of the Magical-Mystical Terms<-
->contained in the Author’s writings,<-
->according to the sense of the Spirit;<-
->as well as<-
->other occurring Latin words.<-

->A<-

**Abba**, Father <note>original: "Abba" (Aramaic/Hebrew term for father, often used in the New Testament to signify intimacy with God).</note>.
**Absentia**, absence, the state of being away.
**Absolviren**, to unbind, to speak loose and free, to forgive sin.
**Absolution**, the release, forgiveness of sins.
**Abstinentia**, abstinence, refraining, moderation.
**Academia**, Academy, the high school <note>original: "hohe Schule," a common 17th-century term for a university.</note>, university.
**Academisch**, in the manner of the high schools or universities.
**Accordiren**, to agree, to be of the same mind.
**Adde**, set or add to <note>original: "Adde" (Latin imperative for "add").</note>.
**Adonai**, the Lord of all things; is a Name of God <note>original: "Adonai" (Hebrew for "my Lord").</note>.
**Adumbriren**, to sketch out, to represent a thing in a draft, painting, or also in writing.
**Advocatus**, an advocate, intercessor, legal representative.
**Advociren**, to speak for someone, to defend someone's cause before a court according to the course of the law.
**Aequanimitas**, equanimity, calmness, steadiness of the mind.
**Aequinoctial-Circul**, the supposed path or circle of the sun in the sky when day and night are of equal length, called "the Line" <note>the Equator</note> by seafarers or sailors.
**Aeternitas**, eternity, a certain time according to the Divine Economy <note>In Böhme’s theology, the "Divine Economy" refers to the specific way God organizes and reveals His will through time and eternity.</note>, eternity.
**Aether**, the natural heaven; it is a degree more subtle than the air.
**Affectus**, affections, passions, all kinds of arousal of the mind, inclinations of the soul, desires, passions.
**Affect-los**, free from desires or affections.

--- Page 11 ---
<meta>This page continues the "First Index" or glossary of terms begun on the previous page. It covers terms from "Affectionate" to "To Appeal," focusing heavily on early scientific (Alchemical, Anatomical) and theological concepts used by Jacob Böhme.</meta>

<page-num>10</page-num>
<header>A. The First Index of</header>

**Affectionate**, favorable, well-disposed.
**Africa**, the 3rd part of the inhabited globe <note>In the 17th century, the world was traditionally divided into three parts: Europe, Asia, and Africa.</note>, containing Egypt and the lands of the Moors, situated toward the south <note>original: "gegen Mittag," literally "toward midday," a common historical term for the South.</note>.
**Alchemy** <term>Alchymia: the art of separating metals through fire, or the art of making gold.</term> It is a hidden science that brings imperfect metals to maturity through their own fire, or transforms lesser metals, such as lead, iron, etc., into genuine gold.
**Alchemist** [Alchymista], such an artist of gold and nature, an alchemist.
**The Alcoran** <note>The Quran</note>, the book of law of the Turks, given to them by Mahomet <note>Muhammad</note>.
**Alexandria**, is a city in Egypt.
**Alphabet** [Alphabetum], the "ABC" in the Greek language, in which *alpha* is the first and *omega* is the last letter. Commonly, this is the name given to the "ABC" of all languages.
**Alumnus**, one who receives discipline, sustenance, and instruction from someone; a pupil.
**Anatomy** [Anatomia], the artistic dissection of corpses, together with a detailed description of all external and internal members of the body.
**Anatomist** [Anatomicus], one who understands and practices such a science.
**To Anatomize**, to artistically dissect dead bodies and lay them out and prepare them for close observation.
**Animalia**, animals, all creatures that have a living soul, like the breath in their nostrils, and can move themselves from place to place.
**Animalish**, soulish, animal-like. The animalish life is the outer natural life in man, which all animals also possess. <note>original: "ἄνθρωπος ψυχικὸς" (Greek: anthrōpos psychikos), referring to the "natural" or "soulish" man in 1 Corinthians 2:14.</note>
Regarding what the author understands by the **animalish spirit** in the work *Aurora*, see *Aurora* chapter 15, paragraph 35.
**Anti-Christ** [Anti-Christus], Antichrist, the Counter-Christ.
**Antimony** [Antimonium], antimony <note>original: "Spies-Glaß," an old term for stibnite or antimony ore</note>, it is a mineral.
**Anno**, in the year.
**Apocalypse** [Apocalypsis], the Revelation of Saint John.
**Apology** [Apologia], a defensive writing, a written accounting or justification to rescue one's honor and innocence.
**To Appeal** [Appelliren], to bring one's case before a higher court when one is not satisfied with the verdict of the lower courts.

--- Page 12 ---
<meta>This page continues the "First Index" or glossary of terms, moving from "Animalish" on the previous page to "Appendix" through "Aspect." It continues to define alchemical, theological, and philosophical terms within the worldview of Jacob Böhme and his contemporaries.</meta>

<page-num>11</page-num>
<header>Theosophical and Latin Words. A.</header>

**Appendix**, the supplement or addition.
**Approbation**, approval, or the applause given when one deems something good.
**Approve** [Approbiren], to favor, to deem good, to sanction.
**Application**, the appropriation or dedication <note>Often referring to how a spiritual truth is applied to the individual soul.</note>.
\* **Aquaster**, a heavenly essence or being formed from heavenly water, containing Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury <note>original: *Sal, Sulphur, Mercurius*. In Paracelsian alchemy, these "Three Principles" compose all matter.</note>.
**Arca, Archa**, the Ark, Noah’s chest.
**Arcanum**, a secret or hidden mystery.
\* **Archaeus** and **Separator**, in the mind, this is a fiery Mercury <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> with a dual effect: the **Archaeus** is the master craftsman and divider of the Essence <note>original: *Entis*</note> out of the Great Mystery <note>original: *Mysterio magno*</note>; the **Separator**, however, divides good and evil, light and dark being from one another, each into its own Principle <note>original: *Principium*</note>.
**Archia**, a principality or high sovereignty.
**Argumentum**, the argument, proof, or basis of a speech.
**Aristotle** [Aristoteles], a pagan world-sage or philosopher in Greece, at the time of Alexander the Great, before the birth of Christ; according to whose principles one usually teaches in schools, especially within the Papacy <note>The author reflects a typical 17th-century Protestant view, skeptical of Aristotle's influence on Catholic scholasticism.</note>.
**Aristotelian**, one who is devoted to his [Aristotle's] opinion.
**Arius**, an erroneous teacher in the 4th century <note>original: *seculo*</note> after Christ’s birth, who denied the eternal birth of the Son of God in the Person of Christ.
**Arian**, one who adheres to such an error.
**Article** [Articulus], a member; also a part of Christian doctrine as it is treated in spiritual or theological books.
**Artist** [Artista], an experienced chemist who possesses the Tincture <note>The "Tincture" was the elusive alchemical substance capable of transmutation.</note>, or the secret of making gold; an adept <note>original: *Adeptus*</note>.
\* **Ascendant**, an ascending star or constellation. (This is also applied spiritually to the mind.)
**Ascension**, the rising up or the going up into heaven.
**Asia**, the second part of the inhabited globe, containing Turkey and the other Eastern lands <note>original: *Morgen-Länder*, literally "morning-lands."</note>.
**Asmodus**, an impure, unchaste spirit; a spirit of frenzy and madness.
**Aspect** [Aspectus], the relative position of the planets when they stand in a certain proportion in the sky—beside, against, or under one another; this is also applied spiritually to the mind.

<meta>This page continues the "First Index" (Erstes Register) of terms, transitioning from the end of the letter "A" into the beginning of the letter "B." It defines astronomical, academic, and biblical terms within the context of 17th-century theosophy.</meta>

<page-num>12</page-num>
<header>A. B. First Index of the</header>

**Astral**, that which is of the nature of the stars and is driven by their power.
**Astrum** <note>original Latin: *Astrum*</note>, a constellation, the starry sky, or the firmament.
**Astrology** <note>original Latin: *Astrologia*</note>, the art of interpreting the stars, or the art of fortune-telling from the position of the constellations.
**Astrologer** <note>original Latin: *Astrologus*</note>, a star-interpreter who recognizes the influence of the firmament from the position of the stars and predicts things in advance.
**Astronomy** <note>original Latin: *Astronomia*</note>, star-lore, the knowledge of the starry sky.
**Astronomer** <note>original Latin: *Astronomus*</note>, a star-knower or star-seer who calculates and measures the outer course, the size, and the distance of the stars. By the Author, **Astrologer** and **Astronomer** are taken as one and the same, namely, as those learned in star-lore.

**Autograph** <note>original Latin: *Autographum*</note>, the handwritten script of an author, the original of a book.
**Author**, the originator, the actual writer and master of a book or another matter.
**Authority**, prestige or standing.

**To form** <note>original: *Formen, formiren*</note>, to mold, to build, to give a shape.
**Former**, a shaper, a Creator.
**Formation** <note>original: *Formirung, Formung*</note>, the building or shaping.
**Formula**, a prescribed way and manner, a rule or instruction.
**Foundation** <note>original: *Fundamentum*</note>, the ground of a thing upon which it stands. <note>The OCR ends with "beste," likely "besteht" (stands/exists).</note>

## G

**Gabriel** <note>original: *Gabri-El*</note>, a man of **GOD**, is the name of an angel who was also sent to the Virgin Mary.
**Gehenna**, hell.
**Gems** <note>original: *Gemma, Gemmen*</note>, precious stones.
**Genesis**, birth, the Creation. This is the name of the First Book of Moses, because it begins with the Creation.
**General Title**, the main name or main title of a book.
**Generation** <note>original: *Generatio*</note>, the procreation, birth.
\* **Genius**, a birth-angel <note>an attendant spirit assigned to a person at birth</note>, is of three kinds: 1) The Genius in the Light, which drives us toward all that is good. 2) The natural Genius in the Fire, which gives a person wit and understanding, with which one governs the outward life. 3) The dark Genius is the *Evectrum* <note>original: *Evektrum*; likely referring to a spectral double or a shadow-spirit</note>.
**Globe** <note>original: *Globus, globul*</note>, the sphere or ball.
**Glory** <note>original: *Gloria*</note>, the honor, splendor.
**Glorification**, the making glorious; **glorified**, made glorious.
**Gloss** <note>original: *Glossa*</note>, a note next to the text, an interpretation.
**Know thyself** <note>original Greek: *Gnothi se auton*</note>.
**Degree** <note>original: *Gradus*</note>, a step, a rung, a stride, a certain measure, or an elevation; **by degrees** <note>original: *gradibus*</note>, according to the steps.
**To graduate** <note>original: *Gradiren*</note>, to elevate, to bring to a measured purpose.
**Grammar** <note>original: *Grammatica*</note>, the art of language, is a treatise on the different kinds of words and their proper use.
**Governor** <note>original: *Gubernator*</note>, a regent, a representative or governor.

## H

\* **Habit** <note>original: *Habitus*</note>, clothing; it is also a state of the mind, where one has grasped a thing well within oneself, a matter that one understands well.
**Thus far he** <note>original Latin: *Hactenus ille*</note>, "so far, up to here that one," namely, the quoted words. <note>A scholarly shorthand indicating the end of a quotation.</note>
**Hallelujah**, praise the **LORD**.
**Harmony** <note>original: *Harmonia*</note>, the agreement, of one mind and spirit.

**Ministry** <note>original: Latin *Ministerium*</note>, the service, the office, <term>also</term> <note>original: Latin *item*</note> the collective number of preachers in a particular place.

**Miracle** <note>original: Latin *Miraculum*</note>, a wondrous work.

**Miserere**, "have mercy." <note>A common liturgical expression, typically referring to the beginning of Psalm 51.</note>

**Model**, any pattern, the blueprint of a thing according to which it is made.

**Tinder** <note>original: *Moder*</note>, actually means any matter in which a small spark can easily catch, be held, and glow, and which can be turned into a burning fire by fanning or blowing; whether it be all sorts of kindling, especially from dry and decayed wood, or ash, wick, and the like. **Glowing tinder** is when a spark is actually present in the kindling or another flammable matter, but cannot yet reach a proper flame.

**Monarch** <note>original: Latin *Monarcha*</note>, a free regent, king, or emperor who rules alone with full power.

**Monarchy** <note>original: Latin *Monarchia*</note>, a free, unrestricted dominion.

**Monster** <note>original: Latin *Monstrum*</note>, a deformity, a monster, or a beast.

**Theosophical and Latin Words. Page 31**

**Paraphrasis** <note>original: *Paraphrasis*</note>, a somewhat detailed interpretation of obscure words and speeches.
**Part** <note>original: *Pars, Part*</note>, the part; **Parts** <note>original: *Partes*</note>, the parts; **By part** <note>original: *Parte*</note>, in the part.
**Particular**, piece-by-piece; also, that which works piece-by-piece. In Chemistry <note>original: *Chymie* - here referring to alchemy</note>, a **Particular** refers to a tincture that transforms only one part of a metal; likewise, one that only acts upon a specific metal but cannot affect others; whereas by contrast, that which acts upon all metals is called "Universal."
**Particularly** <note>original: *Particulariter*</note>, individually, especially.
**Pasquill**, a lampoon or libelous writing.
**Passions** <note>original: *Passiones*</note>, stirrings of the soul <note>original: *Gemüths-Regungen*</note> that arise from the love or anger of nature.
**To Pass** <note>original: *Passiren*</note>, to go by, to travel through.
**Patient**, a sufferer, a sick person, in body or soul.
**Patron** <note>original: *Patronus*</note>, a benefactor, one who takes the place of a father.
**To Pause** <note>original: *Pausiren*</note>, to stop while singing, to keep still.
**To Penetrate** <note>original: *Penetriren*</note>, to pierce through, to comprehend with the understanding, to grasp correctly.
**Persia**, a kingdom in Asia, beyond Turkey <note>original: *Türckey* - at the time of writing, this referred to the Ottoman Empire</note>.
**Fantasy** <note>original: *Phantasia*</note>, imagination, vain thoughts.
**Philautia**, self-love. <note>From the Greek *philautia* (φιλαυτία), often used in a negative sense to mean excessive egoism.</note>
**Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia*</note>, love of wisdom; also, worldly wisdom in all its parts and sciences; **Philosopher** <note>original: *Philosophus*</note>, one who possesses such wisdom, a "world-sage."
**To Philosophize**, to rationally reflect upon natural wisdom.
**Philosophical**, in the manner of the world-sages.
**Phlegm** <note>original: *Phlegma*</note>, a watery moisture.
**Phlegmatic**, of a watery, moist nature; it is one of the four temperaments <note>original: *Complexionen*</note> or qualities of human nature. <note>According to the ancient theory of the four humors, a phlegmatic person was thought to be calm, cool, and perhaps sluggish.</note>
**Phoenix**, may be a secret of nature which the ancients depicted as a bird of incomparable beauty, having no equal and thus living unpaired. It is said to nourish itself only on the pure dew of heaven, and at a great age, to build a nest of the finest spices; after this nest is ignited by the sun's rays, the bird burns itself within it, only to come alive again from the ashes after some time has passed.

# Theosophical and Latin Words. P. 39
### C 4

**Zion** <note>original: *Sion*</note> was a mountain in the city of Jerusalem, upon which David's fortress was built, and subsequently Solomon’s Temple in Jerusalem; the kings of Judah were also buried there. See **Zion**.

**Emerald** <note>original: *Smaragd*</note> is a green gemstone.

* **The Sun** <note>original: *Sol*</note>, is the 4th property of nature, the heart of the life of all properties and the cause of all nature-spirits (except for **Saturn** <note>original: *Saturno*; in this system, Saturn represents contraction and coldness</note>, which is a cause of physicality), just as it also has its seat in the heart of man. With the renewal in man, it creates a mind for itself in which it becomes **tinctural** <note>referring to a "tincture," a spiritual essence that can transform or "color" other substances</note>; it then re-opens the powers of the "spoken word" out of death and hiddenness in the heart. However, it is not a "birthing" of powers, since the outer **Archaeus** <note>a Paracelsian term for the vital formative principle of nature</note> or **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *Spir. M.* or *Spiritus Mundi*</note> is unstable <note>original: *unfix*</note>; what it builds, it breaks apart again, whereby the mind remains a mixed chaos of good and evil, entirely unstable. Therefore, a deeper foundation than that of the Sun must be laid; the spirit must strike the right fire in the soul, where it comes through God the Father to Christ. In metals, the Sun is **Gold**, and its sign is ☉.

**Hungarian Gold** <note>original: *Sol Hungariæ*</note>.

**Tincture of the Sun** <note>original: *Solis Tinctura*</note>, the tincture of the Sun, of Gold, and of the Heart. See **Sol**.

**Solar** <note>original: *Solarisch*</note>, whatever is of the nature and power of the Sun or of Gold.

* **Sophia** <note>Greek for "Wisdom"</note>, the **Wisdom**, is God’s revelation and the physicality of the Holy Spirit, the outflowed word of divine power, knowledge <note>original: *Wissenschaft*</note>, and holiness; the divine "found-ness" and sensitivity, in which the infinite, manifold, and distinct (or dispersed) powers of the **knowledge** <note>original: *Scienz*</note> of the spoken word exist in a **balanced temperament** <note>original: *Temperatur*; meaning a state where all qualities are perfectly harmonized</note>. She is the essential power of the love of God, from which all things have their movement and possibility. She is a passive being and a housing for the working of the love of God and of all humility, which is transmuted equally with the balance. Therefore, she is God’s **Throne of Grace** in man, and a mediator between God [and man...]

This enclosure occurs through the thin will of faith in the Holy Spirit. However, the dark desire of nature impresses <note>The process of "Introduction" or "Impression" where spiritual desire becomes physical density</note> itself, making itself coarse, dark, and hard; the soul must depart from this "impression" again and draw a new will in the light, denying all nature if it wishes to work with **God**.
**Substantial**, essential, graspable.
**Subtle**, delicate, thin.
\* **Sulfur** <note>original Latin: *Sulphur*</note>, <note>alchemical symbol for sulfur: a triangle surmounting a cross</note>, Sulfur, <note>alchemical symbol for sulfur</note>, is in the spirit an essence that divides into two properties according to light and darkness: as *Sul* in joy, and as *Phur* in sorrow <note>A characteristic theosophical folk-etymology: *Sul* represents the light-flame and *Phur* the fiery-anguish</note>. It is the great burning of anguish in the soul until the light rises and separates itself from the darkness. Then each property stands within itself and one is the cause of the other, but they no longer mix.
**Sulfurous**, sulfur-like.
**Sum** <note>original: *Summa*</note>, the total, the content, everything together.
**Summaries**, a brief concept, the contents of a book or chapter.
**Summary**, briefly phrased.
**Superintendent**, a chief overseer, inspector, or bishop, under whose supervision a certain number of other church ministers and the church administration stand.

**To Temper** <note>original German: *Temperiren*</note>, to bring to balance, to moderate, or to still.
**Tempering** <note>original German: *Temperirung*</note>, moderation, the act of equalizing, or formation.

# Theosophical and Latin Words. Z.
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

->Z<-

**Zion** is a paradisiacal essence and the greening of the new body in **Christ**, arising out of the parched soil of nature within us: a dry place <note>original: *dürrer Ort*; Zion is etymologically often linked to the Hebrew word for "dryness" or "parched ground," which the author here contrasts with the spiritual "greening" of the soul</note>.

**Sabaoth** <note>original: *Zebaoth*</note>, hosts, or an angelic multitude. Therefore **God** is called **God Sabaoth**, or the **God of Hosts**—that is, of many armies of angels.

**Zodiac** <note>original Latin: *Zodiacus*</note>, the Circle of Animals <note>original: *Thier-Kreiß*</note> in the heavens; this is the name for that region of the sky where we see the sun throughout the entire year, where the ancient sages indicated the stars through images and figures of animals. This was because the stars only influence the animal or outer soul-spirit—which all animals possess—and bring forth animalistic qualities. There are 12 such starry images in this celestial region, according to the 12 months of the year, as is well known from calendars.

# Theosophical Matters. E.

### III. What the Soul’s Food May Be.

What the soul's spiritual food may be—*The Threefold Life* <note>original: "Pr." / "Drf. L."</note> 23:6; 1:4; *Forty Questions on the Soul* <note>original: "Seel. M."</note> 74:24. How the soul’s nourishment comes from the Word of <term>GOD</term>, *Forty Questions on the Soul* 13. It desires <term>GOD</term> for food, *The Threefold Life* 1:5; eats <term>GOD’S</term> power, 12; must eat the essential Wisdom of God, *Of Holy Baptism* 1:29; must eat the flesh of the Son of Man, as the Divine <term>Being: original "Ens", referring to the spiritual substance or essence of Christ</term>, *Of the Election of Grace* <note>original: "Gnadw."</note> 8:88. How it arrives at the eating of the Divine Essence, *Of the Last Times* <note>original: "Letzte Zeit."</note> 2:21. The animal, mortal soul eats from the <term>Spirit of the World: original "Spir. Mundi", the astral or planetary life-force</term>, while the eternal soul eats from the eternal Word of <term>GOD</term>, *Epistles* 46:18; *Of the Four Complexions* 15, 16. Through earthly eating, it has received an earthly body, *Of Holy Baptism* 1:22. The Word of the <term>Crusher of the Serpent: original "Schlangen-Treter", a reference to Genesis 3:15, representing the inner Christ-power</term> is its new nutriment, 23. The Holy Spirit is the soul’s light, *The Three Principles* 26:10. See *Lord's Supper*.

### IV. Where the Soul Dwells in Man.

Where its seat in the body may be, *The Three Principles* 13:60; chapter 14; *Forty Questions on the Soul* 11. It dwells in the heart and has its governance in the brain, *Forty Questions on the Soul* 8:7, 8. It dwells in the blood, in the <term>Tincture: a spiritual life-essence or "dye" that gives quality to matter</term>, *The Threefold Life* 9:52. The <term>Tincture</term> is its body, the blood its house, *Forty Questions on the Soul* 7:9. It burns from the heart-blood as a kindled light, *The Threefold Life* 14:7. It swims in the perceptible water, in which the eternal water—as the <term>Water-Matrix: the divine spiritual "womb" or source of heavenly substance</term>—is hidden, 18. It hovers between the power of the stars and the elements, *The Three Principles* 7:8. It sits between the kingdoms of hell and the world, chapter 17:71. Why it stands in a prison of the starry and elemental realms, *Of the Last Times* 2:35. It stands between two gates, darkness and light, *The Three Principles* 10:14; between two principles, chapter 12:52. It can live in all three principles, ibid. In a gentle person, it works in harmony <note>original: "inqualiret", a Böhmean term meaning to operate with the same qualities or to be unified in action</note> with the heart of <term>GOD</term>, chapter 13:31. <term>GOD</term> shines through the soul, but it does not grasp Him, *The Threefold Life* 6:86. How they come into the human or the body, *Forty Questions on the Soul* 8. How the soul is held in such union both in the Adamic body and also in the newborn body, *Forty Questions on the Soul* 16.

### VII. On the Circumstances of the Soul / in Regard
### to the Crusher of the Serpent within her.

The word of the <term>Crusher of the Serpent: a title for Christ, referencing the biblical promise in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent’s head</term> is her new <term>Nutriment: spiritual food or nourishment</term>, *On Holy Baptism* 1, chap. 1:23. ## N. III. What her office is in God, angels, and men.

## IV. Where the Tincture lies, and by whom and how it is to be found.

How deeply the Tincture of fire and light lies hidden in all living and growing things, *Theosophical Questions* <note>original: "Theos. Fr." (Theosophische Fragen)</note> 6:15. The Tincture lies in the quintessence of the *Sulphur* <note>original: "Sulphuris" — In Böhme’s "Three Principles" of matter (Salt, Mercury, Sulphur), Sulphur represents the active, fiery, and dark spirit that yearns for the light.</note> or sulfurous spirit, *The Key* <note>original: "Clav."</note> 46. It permeated the earth and the elements before the Fall and tinctured everything, *The Key* 95. It escaped during the Fall of Adam, ibid. **Being, Substantiality** <note>original: "Wesen, Wesenheit." In Böhme’s terminology, "Wesen" refers to the essence or being of a thing, while "Wesenheit" often refers to the spiritual "body" or substantiality of the divine realm.</note>, God is not a "being" but the power for being, *Mysterium Magnum* 6:1. How God brought forth being, and how substantiality originated, *Theosophical Points* 1:42. *Against Stiefel* 353. *Signatura Rerum* 4:21. What heavenly substantiality is, *Threefold Life* 5:68, ch. 8:1/3. *Questions concerning the Soul* 1:212. *The Incarnation of Christ* 1 ch. 3:5, 8. *The Key* 263. The being of all beings is a magical birth from a single [source] into infinity, *Mysterium Magnum* 10:39. Concerning the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterio Magnum." A central Böhme concept referring to the chaos or "unground" from which all creation emerges.</note> of all beings, *Signatura Rerum* 3:1-7.

**Sheet Lightning**, see Flash/Thunder.

**Restoration** <note>original: "Wiederbringung." This refers to Böhme’s hope for the ultimate restoration of all things to their original divine state.</note> of all that Adam lost is like the eternal birth and the process of the Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: "Lapidis Philosophorum." Böhme uses the language of alchemy to describe the spiritual transformation of the soul from a base, "fallen" state into a "golden," divine state.</note>, *Signatura Rerum* 7:78.

**Counter-Christ**, see Antichrist.

**Adversity** <note>original: "Wiederwärtigkeit." Also translated as "opposition" or "contrariety." Böhme believed that without the friction of opposing forces, nothing could be revealed or made manifest.</note>, without adversity nothing may be revealed to him, *Divine Contemplation* 1:8. The adversity of all beings, how one is the "loathing" <note>original: "Eckel." In this context, it refers to the natural repulsion or clash between opposing qualities (like light and dark) that generates life and movement.</note> of the other, *Earthly and Heavenly Mystery* 6:1. It is in the creature, 2. From this originates all the power of this world, 3.

**Rebirth** <note>original: "Wiedergeburt." This is likely a primary heading whose sub-entries continue on the following page.</note>.

# ERRATA
## or Printer’s Errors.

**Note.** <note>original: "Nota"</note> **Page** or **p.** means the side of the leaf, **l.** <note>original: "lin. linea"</note> means line, **§.** <note>original: "paragraphus"</note> means paragraph or verse, **S.** means **Summaries** or Contents, **f.** for, **l.** <note>original: "lies"</note> read, **ib.** <note>original: "ibidem"</note> in the same place, **l. ult.** <note>original: "ultima"</note> the last line, **l. pen.** <note>original: "penultima"</note> the second line from the bottom, **l. ant.** <note>original: "antepenultima"</note> the third line from the bottom, **a.** <note>original: "adde"</note> add or set down, **d.** <note>original: "dele"</note> delete or strike out. Otherwise, the second number after two dots (:) indicates the **Paragraph**, and the third number after a comma (,) indicates the line of that paragraph.

### Main Title.

Line 11. for **Writings** <note>original: "Schriften"</note> read **Treasures**. <note>original: "Schätzen"</note>

### Preface.

Page 17. l. 9. for **bring** read **provide**; p. 31. line 20. f. **of the same** [feminine/plural] read **of the same** [masculine/neuter]; p. 33. l. 20. f. **strike out** <note>original: "ausschlagen"; can also mean to refuse</note> read **open up**. <note>original: "aufschlagen"</note>

Page 1. **Summaries** l. 17. for **Precaution** <note>original: "Vorsorge"</note> read **Solicitude** <note>original: "Umsorge"</note>; p. 6 : 21, [line omitted] for **these** read **the**; p. 15 : 67, 3. f. **transfigured** read **explained**; p. 35 : 31, 2. after **behold** add **GOD**; p. 125 : 60, 4. f. **deceives** <note>original: "berüget," likely a typo for "betrüget"</note> read **reproved** <note>original: "gerüget"</note>; p. 140 : 63 / 3. f. **and** read **nor**; p. 167. l. 5. from the bottom, after **has** add **here**; p. 191 : 18, 5. f. **nearest** <note>original: "mächste," likely a typo for "nächste"</note> read **most powerful**; p. 221. l. 4. from the bottom, f. **also** read **House**; p. 226. l. 1. f. **yet** read **also**; p. 227 : 32, 3. after **his** add **beautiful**; p. 239. **Summaries** l. 11. f. **bears** <note>original: "gebäret"</note> read **built** <note>original: "gebauet"</note>; p. 256 : 78, 2. after **an** add **old**; p. 279 : 90 / 5. f. **and** read **in**; p. 285. **Summaries** l. 7. f. **The** [feminine] read **The** [masculine]; p. 303 l. **pen.** <note>second line from bottom</note> after **between** add **the wrath of GOD and between**; p. 308 : 59, 1. after **I** add **also**; p. 320. l. 10. f. **a** read **in the**; p. 341 : 24, 1. f. **fourth** read **four-**; p. 344 : 47, 2. **delete** the; p. 346 : 58, 3. f. **and last** read **the last**; p. 352 : 94, 4. f. **waste** <note>original: "wüsten"</note> read **earnest** <note>original: "ernsten"</note>; p. 384. **Summaries** l. **ant.** <note>third line from bottom</note> after **the** add **first**.

--- Page 464 ---
<meta>This page transitions from the errata (printing corrections) found on the previous page to a technical "Report to the Bookbinder." It provides specific instructions for assembling the various treatises of Jacob Böhme into a single collection, ensuring that the complex pagination and signatures do not lead to errors during the binding process. The catchword "nung" from the previous page's "Ord-" completes the word "Ordnung" (order) on the following page.</meta>

# Report
## to the
# Bookbinder,

Concerning **Jacob Böhme’s** writings / for whose owners some reminders may likewise serve as helpful information.

---

->I.<-

The <term>treatises</term> <note>original: "Tractate"</note> each have—and sometimes several small ones together—their own <term>pagination</term> <note>original: "Pagina"</note> and <term>signature mark</term>, <note>original: "Signatur"; the letters or numbers at the bottom of a page used to guide the binder in folding and nesting the sheets.</note> which, however, are primarily distinguished from one another by the <term>running head</term> <note>original: "Column-Titel"</note> at the top; there, the accompanying Roman numeral also indicates the order of the books. Therefore, the bookbinder, when <term>collating</term> <note>original: "Collationiren"; the process of checking that all sheets are present and in the correct order.</note> during the stitching, must not only look at the page and signature—which are the same in all treatises—but **NB.** <note>Latin: "Nota Bene" or "Note Well."</note> primarily at the <term>catchword</term>, <note>original: "Custos"; the word printed at the very bottom of a page that is meant to match the first word of the following page.</note> which will ensure he does not go astray or bind anything incorrectly; as every binder should already know and practice this as a matter of course.

->II.<-

The copies are all diligently collated before being sent out, so that nothing will easily be missing; thus, he and his assistants must take care that <term>defects</term> <note>original: "Defecte"; referring here to missing pages or signatures in a volume.</note> are not created through carelessness or negligence, just as one often hears accurate booksellers complain in this regard. Accordingly, a clear list shall be given here of what belongs to these present complete works, and how everything is to be placed in its proper or-

# Notice
## to the Reader.

**A**fter this improved and enlarged edition of all the writings of the late <note>original: "seligen" — a traditional way of referring to a deceased person, similar to "the late" or "of blessed memory."</note> Jacob Böhme was completely prepared, many expressed regret that the copperplates <note>Symbolic engravings used to illustrate mystical concepts.</note>—which had been added to various treatises in the Amsterdam printing of the year 1682—were to be omitted this time; they believed that the completeness of this new edition would suffer in such a way. Now, although it has already been mentioned in the "Reminder" <note>A term for a preface or introductory note.</note> placed at the front of the present edition on pages 29 and 30 how matters stand regarding these copperplates—which everyone who wishes to read these writings might well consider—another friend has finally judged that those who are against these plates could not interpret it so poorly if, despite such a warning, one were to grant the wish of those seekers <note>original: "Liebhabern" — literally "lovers," referring to the "Lovers of Truth" or dedicated students of Böhme’s theosophy.</note> who nevertheless desired to have the external copperplates included. As these plates are now herewith delivered to them—since they can, at the very least, serve as an ornament to these writings, even if they should not originate from the Author’s own spirit <note>The publisher is clarifying that Böhme himself did not design these illustrations; they were created by later followers to explain his visions.</note>—these figures have likewise been provided with the explanations which were made and attached there by the inventors of each plate. However, we have preferred to have them all printed here together; and these pages may, at one's pleasure, be placed either immediately after the main title or bound at the back with the triple index. In this manner, no one will henceforth be able to say that the present edition is deficient in this regard because of the beautiful copperplate engravings now added. I also heartily wish, however, that everyone may make a right use of them.

## Explanation of the Figure
### for the Main Title.

Just as the whole of Holy Scripture—which flowed from God’s mouth through His holy teachers, prophets, and apostles—consists almost entirely of figures, hidden prophetic speeches, riddles, and histories alongside the singular teaching purpose of repentance and godliness, so too do the wonders of Divine Wisdom truly appear within them. They recount the past, model the present, and signal the future; however, they do so in such a way that neither coarse, fleshly reason nor self-important, "clever" <note>The German "eigenwizige" implies a person who thinks they are wise but lacks true spiritual insight.</note> intellect can understand or guess them at first glance. In this way, the secrecy of Divine Wisdom maintains its dignity, and cause is given only to the wise and understanding heart to "dig deep" and search for it. Just as externally the beautiful and shining gold—as the noblest body or essence of all nature—is dug out of the dark and coarse earth according to Solomon’s proverb, Proverbs 3:14, so too does one find in these writings of Divine Revelation such a depth and richness of wisdom that all human reason is overwhelmed by it. One need only consider the "Philosophical Sphere" or the "Wonder-Eye of Eternity" in the *Forty Questions*; likewise the "Wheel of Nature" in the *Threefold Life*, and then the secret interpretation of the end of time in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>—to say nothing of what remains wrapped up here and there throughout the writings.

From these writings, we have perceived through Divine Grace the ideal form of this spirit <note>Meaning the spiritual essence or "genius" behind Böhme’s revelations.</note>, as the gift of revelation for this time, and have presented it to the lovers of wisdom <note>original: "Liebhabern der Weißheit" — refers to the "Philo-sophi" or students of Böhme’s theosophy.</note> for further reflection in the first figure of the title of all his works. To provide an interpretation of the same is as impossible in this brief space as it is unnecessary to set down, because within the writings

These form a single sphere in Eternity, and yet in their essence they are distinct and stand back-to-back against one another.

So too are the 12 numbers of the hours indicated in these writings, in which the following is to be noted. The [number] 12, which stands at the very top outside the circle in the *vertex* <term>vertex: the highest point or summit</term> or peak of the clock-circle, signifies firstly the Godhead, as the beginning of all beings, or the Majesty [with] crown and scepter, without change or movement—incomprehensible to the creature because it is a Spirit. [Going] straight downwards through the cross symbol †, the 7th number designates the [substantiality] or the holy element of the Divine [Being], from which all things are created. Secondly, [it points to] the first single man, Adam, whom God [created in a] clarified body of light or paradisiacal quality, and appointed as king or ruler over all creatures, as the 8th Psalm says: *You have put all things under [his feet].* But because he [abandoned] the Unity of God, the true wisdom, and lusted after [worldly] cleverness and [the knowledge] where evil and good are mixed, the spirit of visible nature seized him and led him into the wheel of time and vanity, so that he has fallen from [his] height and dignity: as the spirit [witnesses] even this hour, and until the end of time, etc.

...though it portrays it, it is neither considered nor understood by anyone. Thirdly, it signifies the name **JESUS**, as the highest love of God’s unity, who gave Himself into the death of fallen humanity and birthed it back to life. He has reconquered the lost kingdom of man, ascended to heaven, and has once again taken up the royal **place** <note>original: "Locum"</note> of Paradise. He now reigns in the spirit of the faithful and, after the completion of time, will reign with them as their King and Divine Monarch of peace for all eternity.

Fourthly, there are many other interpretations of the prefigurations of Christ in the patriarchs—Isaac, Jacob, Judah, Joseph, etc.—which are to be found in their designated places.

The following circle downwards on the left-hand side, where the numbers **2** and **3** are enclosed, is separated from the uppermost, brightly shining circle so that it does not touch it. Along with the circles that follow, it already signifies the doubled or divided properties of fallen human nature, which is the reality of malice. This can be seen in **Cain**, the second human being, who set himself above **Abel**, the third human, out of pride, ambition, and envy, and murdered him. Thus, this lineage took possession of the world through the **Sword of Vengeance**, and through all ages, the longer it lasted, the more fertile it became in the curse upon the earth.

However, the fact that the rays from the uppermost circle still penetrate this one signifies the incarnate Word of Grace in the covenant of the promise of the **Serpent-Crusher** <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter," a traditional German reference to the "Seed of the Woman" in Genesis 3:15 who would crush the head of the serpent</note>, representing the holy and pious mind of Abel and all subsequent holy patriarchs, teachers, and prophets.

The **Eye** in the center-point of the clockwork and the pointer—set within the fiery triangle, enclosed by a threefold watery triangle, and surrounded by a glow of light—signifies the **Eye of God**. It also represents the eye of man in the **Holy Ternary** <note>original: "Ternario Sancto"; in the author's mystical system, this refers to the three-fold manifestation of God within the created world</note>, through which God sees and man reveals the mysteries of God and His will according to the form of this time. It shows how close time has run to its end, and that the **seventh trumpet** is now being sounded, so that the mystery of the Kingdom of God shall be completed and made manifest when **Babel** <note>representing the confused, fallen world-system and false religious structures</note> is swallowed up by the fiery sword of the **Turba** <note>original: "Turbæ"; Böhme’s technical term for the "spirit of disturbance" or the awakening of divine wrath that consumes vanity and falsehood</note>, and all the curse of vanity is consumed.

It concludes with a description of the "Eye of God" within the Holy Ternary, which signals the approaching end of the age and the destruction of the worldly "Babel."</summary>

# Explanation of the Figure

The alphabet circling within signifies the **Nature-Language** <term>Natur-Sprache: Böhme’s concept that the true essence of things is expressed through the sounds and letters of their names</term>, about which the wonders of God are sufficiently explained in the *Mysterio Magno* <term>Great Mystery: Böhme’s 1623 commentary on Genesis</term> and other indicated places, and it is not necessary to <unclear>mention</unclear> anything further here.

Yet, according to the degree of preeminence or guidance <note>original: "Fü-," likely "Führlichkeit"</note> of the Good, all formation happens through the **†** <note>the symbol of the Cross</note>, which is the primary ground of all **Signature** <term>Signatur: the outward markings that reveal an object’s inner spiritual nature</term> or order <unclear>order</unclear> of the Eternal, Divine, and Temporal Birth <note>original: "Geb-," likely "Geburt"</note> and Being; in Up and Down, in Above and Below, in Light <note>original: "L-," likely "Licht"</note> and Darkness, in Spirit and Body, in Life and Death, [Fire?] and Water, in Air and Earth, etc.

Finally, this is still to be noted regarding the Author’s <note>original: "Autori-," likely "Autoris"</note> figure of the **Philosophical Sphere** in the *40 Questions* <term>referring to Böhme’s work "Forty Questions on the Soul"</term>, where the **Principles** are placed or situated in reverse. ## Title-Figure I for the *Aurora*.

**W**hen a double dawn breaks at midnight, and two suns rise at once, then a great glorious day is at hand, and the Bridegroom is already approaching.
<note>The "double dawn" and "two suns" are prophetic metaphors for a spiritual awakening that occurs even in the darkest times (midnight), signaling the return of Christ, the Bridegroom.</note>

Six days are appointed for labor and sorrow, wherein one may indeed draw breath so that life and strength may be maintained, but not rest until the evening of the sixth is passed, nor rejoice until the seventh has begun.

And before that comes, all the works of the six days from the first to the last will be gathered and brought before the eyes of the Lord, who looks exactly through all places for what is corrupted, forgotten, and neglected, so that He may measure out to each his reward according to his work; for in the seventh, everything that was wrought in the six days must stand in full view.

### Explanation II.

[who] knows how to speak of joys, who has felt no suffering, or of peace, who has seen or experienced no strife?

Thus, opposition <note>original: *Wiederwärtigkeit*; in Böhme’s terminology, this refers to the necessary tension or "counter-stroke" required for the hidden God to become manifest and perceptible.</note> is a revelation of the equanimity <note>original: *Gleichheit*; the state of undifferentiated stillness or "sameness" in the Godhead before creation.</note>, which hovers within itself insensibly in the silent eternity, without light, without darkness, without joy, without sorrow.

But from where does opposition enter into the same and silent eternity, which knows, perceives, or possesses nothing outside of itself?

Where one wishes to have something that is not there, such desire <note>original: *Begierde*; a central concept in Böhme's thought, where the "will" of the abyss contracts to create the first stirrings of nature.</note> creates anxiety and woe. Thus, a hidden life gives no joy; and since the solitary eternity has nothing outside itself, it seeks the delight of its own revelation within itself, for power, might, and glory—indeed, everything—lies within its bosom. Dark hell and bright light echo from one heart through the Word according to the Scripture: *I form the light, and create darkness, I make peace, and create evil. I am the Lord, who does all these things,* so that one may know from the rising of the sun and from its setting, that there is none besides me. Isaiah 45:6-7.

And therefore the all-singular freedom divides itself, and yet remains an undivided, gentle unity. It seeks light and power, and through desire, makes itself into anxiety and darkness. Thus, it births itself out of the darkness into the light, for the darkness awakens the fire, and the fire the light, and the light reveals the wonders of wisdom in images and figures, which it led from its gentle freedom (from the mirror of wisdom and wonders) into the dark desire, where they had been hidden. All of this is explained through Divine Revelation from the eternal depth in this book, Chapter 1: 15; ch. 3: 12, 13; ch. 4: 18, 46, 47, 48, 50 to 53, 58 to 62, 65 to 76; ch. 5: 7, 8, 9, 10, 13 to 18, 21, 25, 27, 28, 31; ch. 6: 2, 5, 14; ch. 7: 8, 9, 14, 15, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 34; ch. 8: 3, 7, 16, 19, 20, 23; ch. 9: 30; ch. 17: 51, 52, 104; ch. 18: 19; ch. 22: 14, 25, 26; ch. 24: 29; ch. 27: 8. ## Title-Figure III. for the *Threefold Life*.

Every work, in its form, essence, and property, reveals the understanding and the virtue of its maker. When one gazes upon the great and wondrous structure of the visible heavens and the earth, considers their movements, searches out the various effects of their powers, and weighs the differences in the bodies of creatures—how they are hard, soft, coarse and subtle, dark and shining, thick and clear, heavy and light—one finds the twofold mother of God's revelation: the **darkness** and the **light**. These have breathed themselves out from all their powers and sealed wonders, forming themselves together with the firmament, stars, elements, and all visible, tangible creatures, where life and death, good and evil, exist together in every thing. This is the **Third** of the two hidden lives, and it is called **Time in the conflict of vanity**. <note>original: *Zeit im Streit der Eitelkeit*; Böhme views the physical world as a temporary "Third Life" where the eternal principles of Light/Heaven and Darkness/Hell are locked in a visible struggle.</note>

Here Wisdom <note>Referring to *Sophia*, the divine mirror or feminine principle of God's self-reflection.</note> shines through, in which the Holy Spirit opens the Divine powers with images of angels and humans; it shines everywhere through the sun, moon, and stars, through gold, silver, ore, precious stones, through beautiful colors and scents—indeed, through every good part in all creatures, and especially in the understanding, love, justice, benevolence, gentleness, chastity, knowledge of God, discipline, art, and virtue of mankind.

Here also the property of hell and darkness manifests itself through cold, hardness, earth, stones, blackness, poison, and stench in all creatures; and in mankind through malice, hatred, folly, wrath, unchastity, godlessness, outrage, stupidity, and vice.

Thus this world stands in the mixed life of Time between light and darkness, as a living mirror of them both, in which the wonders of eternity become manifest in the form of time through the Word, as John reports: All

### Explanation V. 2.

The bow is drawn, and an arrow is aimed at you; there was great love for you, and great anguish and sorrow over you. You could not remain hidden, for you were a royal heir and were meant to possess the throne. You were intended to rule over the animals, but not to lust after their flesh, nor to touch their soul in the blood, for they were unclean before you, and their spirit was merely a game within the **wonder of vanity.** <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "wonder of vanity" refers to the temporary, illusory nature of the physical world created after the Fall.</note> You were not to love them at all; for love is a fire, and it possesses the power of formation in its root, such that it shapes itself into the likeness of the beloved.

But because he <note>Referring to the spirit of the world or the "Behemoth" of earthly desire.</note> wooed you so much, you allowed yourself to be beguiled and laid your head in his lap and fell securely asleep. Thus, your light went out, and your power and strength were taken from your head, and you were swallowed by the <term>Behemoth</term> <note>A biblical beast representing the raw, monstrous power of the material or fallen nature.</note> into his belly. Then all his young came forth from their caves and nests and wanted to gorge themselves on your flesh: fierce bears, greedy wolves, angry lions, haughty stallions and peacocks, envious dogs, gluttonous pigs, lecherous goats, cunning snakes, raging dragons, poisonous toads, stinging spiders, evil adders, coarse oxen, stupid donkeys, fearful hares, bold falcons, predatory eagles—all the worms of the earth and all the flying swarms in the air had power over you. There was none that knew you or spared you, for you were a stranger in their forest.

Then your Mother, Love, spoke in her heart: "Who will rescue my son and snatch my heir from the jaws of the beasts? I will arise early and disguise myself as a beast; I will give my life as a <term>ransom</term> <note>original: "Ranzion," an archaic term for the price paid to liberate a prisoner.</note> for his life, so that I may redeem him and restore him to honor."

Thus the Heart of **GOD** shaped itself in the sweet name **JESUS** into a meek, innocent Lamb, once our distress was recognized, so that he might rescue us from sin, death, and the pain of hell under the form of a similar object through his blood. This is witnessed in *Isaiah 53* and by *Peter* in his first epistle, *Chapter 1, verse 20.* These deep mysteries in Divine Revelation are particularly explained in these writings: *Chapter 6:9, Chapter 9:3.* In the preceding Part 1, *Chapter 5:23,* and further in ***The Three Principles***, *Chapter 18:25, Chapter 17:107, 108,* and ***The Threefold Life***, *Chapter 5:98.*

V. 3. of the Engravings.

# Title Figure V. 3. of the Third Part of *The Incarnation of Christ* / The Tree of Faith.

Fire is the root of life for all creatures, and if that fire is lost, one seeks it in steel, stone, and tinder, which are nonetheless all born from fire. <note>Böhme uses "fire" as a metaphor for the fundamental driving force or "soul-center" of existence. Just as we strike a flint to find hidden fire, we must seek the hidden divine spark in a world that seems cold.</note> So it is also with life: when it is disrupted and filled with conflict, its powers divide and go into a state of separation, so that each power performs its own specific office.

Had we remained in childlike simplicity and obedience to the Word, and in the contemplation of Divine Wisdom in Paradise, then faith and hope would have remained hidden, and love alone would have been manifest. <note>In the state of perfection, "faith" is unnecessary because one already "sees" and "possesses" God; Böhme argues these virtues only exist because we are currently separated from our source.</note> Now it is the reverse, because we have turned outward toward the starry region <note>The "starry region" refers to the physical, astral world and the rational mind influenced by it, which Böhme believed clouded our spiritual perception.</note>, which covers and dulls the lovely light-flames of love for us; thus we must believe and hope for what we neither see nor feel, until the love of God rekindles our deadened love and gives birth to it anew within itself for life.

Therefore faith, as a hidden flame, proceeds from "starry reason" upward through the death of Christ to produce the fruits of love and the Spirit; and it roots itself downward in humility through hope. Hope, however, does not grasp at the earthly, but lifts its wings with faith toward God above.

Thus the new growth pushes out from God through Hell and Nature, through malice and reason, until it is transplanted into its proper field of the heavenly body. Then faith and hope enter into the <term>Mysterium</term> <note>original: "Mysterium." In this context, it refers to the hidden, spiritual reality or the "Great Mystery" of God's being.</note> of the new spirit born in God, which is manifest in love and united with God. It is then no longer called faith, but **Contemplation** <note>Beschaulichkeit; here meaning the direct mystical vision of God.</note>; no longer hope, but **Possession** and **Enjoyment** of life in the peace and joy of the Holy Spirit, as is taught here: Chapter 2: 1. c. 3: 5. c. 6: 5. 6. 8. c. 7: 5. 6. 7. c. 8: 6. 7. In the preceding second part, c. 6: 10. And following in *The Threefold Life*, c. 6: 31. 32.

## Title Figure VIII. of the Earthly and Heavenly Mystery.

All earthly and perishable creatures that dwell in various places within the elements are sealed wonders. They lie within the great spirit and life of the world, which first reveals its specific mysteries through the constellations <note>original: "Gestirne"</note> from the one fountain of the sun. From these, the manifold variety of spirits, bodies, shapes, and colors of all creatures are then formed and fashioned, each according to the property of its own star-influence <note>original: "Astri"; Böhme refers to the spiritual force or "signature" exerted by the stars on physical matter.</note> within the weaving of the elements. In its entire form, this manifest world—with the sun and the stars—is a reflection and a modeling after the Eternal Mystery. There, the Spirit opens through the Word in the Light the innumerable wonders seen in the contemplation of Divine Wisdom. It reveals the Divine Kingdom in ideas, images, and figures from the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Ungrund"; Böhme’s central concept of the "groundless" or "bottomless" nothingness that exists before God’s self-manifestation.</note> of the Eternal Unity. Every flowing property is in itself a particular <term>Sacred Mystery</term> <note>original: "Arcanum"; a secret or hidden spiritual power.</note> of a particular <term>Knowledge</term> <note>original: "Scienz"; here meaning a structured spiritual wisdom or branch of divine understanding.</note>, and it proceeds out of itself with the <term>Fire-Center</term> <note>The "Fire-Center" is the driving, energetic core of an individual being's desire to exist.</note> of its own desire to reveal its wonders. Thus, the <term>Abyss</term> of Eternal Freedom is filled with eternal life and movement in innumerable wonders. As may be seen here in Text 4. §. 1. 2. 3. 6. 7. 8. Text 5. §. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Text 7. §. 1. 2. 3. 4. 6. 7. 8. 9. 10. And following in *The Three Principles*, c. 25: 31. 65. *The Incarnation of Christ*, c. 1: 9. 10 11. 12. c. 2: 1. 2. *The Small Six Points*, c. 3: 7. 8. 9. 12. 13 14. 15. 16. 17. 18. *Christ’s Testament of Baptism*, c. 1: 4 to 22. *Divine Contemplation*, c. 1: 23. 24. 25. 26. 27. c. 2: 2. to 9. 12. 13. 22. 25. 26. 29. c. 3: 1. 5. to 12. 14. 17. 18. 19. 41. c. 4: 2. to 6.

### IX. The Engraving.

With fire you entered into a false lodging, and with fire you must break out again; otherwise, the cunning and evil guardians who lie in wait for your life will hold you captive, seeking to kill you and lock you away in the grave.

Below, you will find no exit, for your earthly desire presses you ever more tightly together the longer it lasts, and your root reaches far and deep out of great hunger, seeking refreshment <note>original: "Labsal"; a restorative comfort or healing drink.</note> in the earth, though there is none to be found in the darkness. The deeper the root seeks, the greater the hunger becomes, for nourishment is born only in the light and the water.

Only from above (beyond all the senses) in the air does one draw breath and strengthen life. Even if dark clouds should cover your light and make your path dim, simply hold fast to hope with long-suffering and patience: after the night comes the day, and after the harsh winter comes the lovely summer. It awakens the little grain of wheat <note>A common mystical metaphor for the soul’s potential, derived from John 12:24.</note> from death and, through the gentle rain, brings forth grain, wine, and oil in abundance, so that your heart may be strengthened, your soul refreshed, and your spirit rejoiced in life forever and ever. Regarding this, see also the following books after this little volume: *On Resignation* <note>original: "Gelassenheit"</note>, chapter 1:12, 42; chapter 2:38, 39, 40. *On Regeneration* <note>original: "Wiedergeburt"</note>, chapter 4:1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 12, 13; chapter 5:10 to 14. *Aurora* <note>The Day-Spring</note>, chapter 20:46, 49 to 54. *The Three Principles* <note>original: "Drey Principia"</note>, chapter 17:34, 80, 104; chapter 24:8, 12, 13, 20, 23, 24, 35, 36, 40, 43; chapter 25:3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12; Appendix, 36. *The Threefold Life* <note>original: "Dreyfaches Leben"</note>, chapter 7:12, 13; chapter 8:6; chapter 11:63, 64, 65; chapter 14:4, 7, 8, 16, 17:20, 21, 23, 24, 25, 27, 34, 35, 36, 41; chapter 16:4, 15. *Forty Questions*, Question 11: 2, 3. ## Title-Figure IX. b. Concerning Re-birth <note>original: "Wieder" [Wiedergeburt]</note>

The † <note>The symbol of the Cross.</note> is the birth of all things, the † is the rebirth, though to reason it is a foolishness <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 1:23, where the cross is described as foolishness to the Greeks.</note> and a strange wonder-speech, because reason is born from the starlit, natural sunshine and does not yet know the eternal death that sticks in its root. Whoever feels this sting becomes aware of the great distress, so that like David he must anxiously sigh: *Out of the depths I cry to you* <note>original: "Aus der Tieffe ruff ich zu dir"; Psalm 130:1.</note>. For he sees that his will is corrupted, inclined to pride and malice, and rebellious against God; therefore he cries out for the rebirth of a new spirit.

## Title-Figure IX. c. Concerning the Super-Sensual Life. <note>original: "überlichen Leben"; referring to a life lived above the level of the five senses.</note>

Manifold creatures awaken manifold desires / 
and he who has manifold desires and loves much / 
is in turn loved, enticed, pushed, 
driven, and turned around by many things.

But what is the end of this other than distraction / 
constant anxiety and aversion, which his reason 
shapes and forms for him in animalistic and transitory pleasures and desires / 
which death consumes; and thus neither the Divine Love of Unity, nor the single image / 
is known.

Therefore, it would help us nothing even if we had the power of all the stars / 
and of all the animals, in senses, thought, 
cleverness, power, pleasure and joys, in the use of 
manifold creatures, and yet lost our own image / 
in which we were formed from God and after God / 
so that we might recognize Him, behold Him, and love Him alone.

But blessed is he who uses the power that is 
granted to him anew in Christ, that he might turn his will 
out of the whirlpool-point <note>original: "Wirbel-Punct"; a term used by Jakob Böhme to describe the restless, churning center of the soul’s desires before it finds peace in the Divine light.</note> of the love of all creatures / 
into the death of Christ: For it is better that the eye 
of offense be plucked out, and the soul look with but One eye 
into the Unity of God in the light, and behold the eternal life / 
than with two eyes behold the discord and multiplicity 
of nature and creature, whereby she is scattered in her will / 
ignited and captured in the desire for pleasure / 
and thus in spirit puts on an animalistic deformity / 
wherein she can never behold God nor find the bliss / 
that consists only in His contemplation and Unity / 
according to the Scripture: I will behold your face 
in righteousness, I will be satisfied when I awake. <note>A reference to Psalm 17:15.</note>

## Title-Figure IX. d. Regarding the Dialogue between the Enlightened and Unenlightened Souls.

Wandering costs the little crown of honor <note>original: "Ehrenkränzlein"; a symbol of spiritual purity or the "virgin" state of the soul before it is corrupted by worldly desires.</note> and a beautiful inheritance, which the harlots devour.

You have indeed taken only one step beyond your boundary, but you have come far into distant islands and deserts of the heathens, who do not know the God of Israel nor sanctify His name.

Now you sweat anxiety in your great sorrow, distress, and heartache: For instead of bread and wine, which grows abundantly on the mountains of your Father, you seek only husks <note>original: "Träbern"; refers to the pods or draff eaten by the swine in the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15:16).</note>, and in your hunger, you must still go without even those. Moreover, the way to your fatherland is lost, and barred with earth, water, air, and fire <note>The four elements represent the material world that imprisons the spiritual soul.</note>, so that you find nothing but greed, envy, pride, and wrath, which torment you without ceasing and keep you captive in the belly of the snakes.

Now you see where you have wandered, since your heavenly body is transformed into animal flesh, and your Divine Paradisiacal dwelling is changed into stellar torment. <term>stellar torment (Sternen-Qual)</term> <note>In Böhmean mysticism, this refers to the "astral" influence of the stars which subjects the soul to the conflicting, restless forces of the material universe.</note>

Therefore, it is not good to hold conversation with the Devil and the snakes, nor to follow their counsel: For in their mouth is nothing certain, their inward part is heartache, their throat is an open grave, and they flatter with their tongues. Psalm 5.

But Love carries the power of life in the Word of the Cross and breaks the gates of death and hell through its entrance into the flesh, so that it might give us new birth through the spirit of simplicity and open the way to Paradise, so that we shall live eternally in our fatherland in new obedience, in the peace and joy of the Holy Spirit, according to His good pleasure: As is to be found in this dialogue; and further in the following: *The Three Principles*.

Such things stir your wrath, so that when your throne is shown to be of hell and your crown is seen in the thick fog, you swing open your maw and wish to shatter the mirror <note>The "Mirror of Wisdom" or the "Mirror of God" is a common mystical term for the divine reflection or revelation that shows things as they truly are.</note> and stain it with blasphemy.

But your smoke does not endure in this light; it recoils and seeks you in the abyss. You must suffocate from this radiance, be blinded, and be put to eternal shame. Your false appearance is recognized, for it is no shining light that originates from the single center of Divine Birth; rather, it is the confused rays of many centers that run cross-wise through and against one another in madness, quarreling, strife, disgrace, slander, blasphemy, conflict, and war, to destroy the earth, and

## Title-Figure XIV. regarding the *Signature of All Things*. <note>original: *Signatura Rerum*. This is Böhme’s theory that the internal spirit of a thing is "signed" or manifested in its external form.</note>

There is but a single character <note>A spiritual mark or seal.</note> by which the Deity has imaged Himself, and with the same He has also marked every creature, so that His presence is in everything; and yet, every creature has its own particular sign, figure, and form, so that it may appear as a special wonder of the heavenly or earthly Mystery <note>original: *Mysterii*</note>. # Title-Figure XV. regarding the Election by Grace <note>Election by Grace (Gnaden-Wahl) refers to the theological debate over how God chooses who is saved; Böhme argues that it is tied to the human will's response to divine light.</note>

The first origin of all things is only one Will, Alpha and Omega <note>original: "A und O"</note>, a beginning without beginning, an infinite Something: it reveals itself through its anxious sharpness of the dark desire with the outpouring into Power, Light, Joy, Glory, and the Wonders of Wisdom, and breathes itself into names, parables, and figures through angels and men for its own contemplation.

Thus the created will of man is a likeness of the eternal, uncreated Will of God; it has Fire from God’s Fire, and Light from God’s Light, for the revelation of His wonders within itself, and is, after its creation, its own little god and judge: what it wills and works, its **Fiat** <note>The Latin command "Let it be." Böhme uses this to describe the creative, shaping power of the soul's will.</note>—which it is itself—creates for it, and judges it with witness in its work and formation according to its choice: in the Good with light, power, and joys, in the knowledge of God, virtue, and songs of praise; in the Evil with darkness, malice, and anxiety in godlessness, sin, and vice.

But because the human will, through the Fall into this corrupted nature, is burdened and seduced by the temptation of vanity within itself, so that it seizes upon evil even in ignorance, Death is the boundary-mark of separation. It places the Word of Life, which became human, in the center as a mirror; it gives the will power, light, and knowledge to depart from its defilement, just as the sun does for the plants of the earth. Whoever now wishes to grasp it through repentance <note>original: "Busse"</note> will be grasped, and today (that is, in this very "Now" and the light of grace) is led through death—which the will accepted in sin through temptation—into Paradise.

But he who despises it in malice and mocks grace, to him the Word becomes mute, and works no promise of life in his perverted will, because he loves obduracy <note>A state of being stubborn or "hardened" against God's influence.</note> and chooses death.

Thus the Election by Grace is understood within the actual desire for grace, according to the word in Revelation <note>original: "Apoc."</note> 22. He who

## Title-Figure XVI. regarding Christ's Testaments. <note>The "Testaments" refer to the two sacraments of the Lutheran tradition: Holy Baptism and the Lord's Supper.</note>

When one eats an evil, poisonous fruit, the food consumes the eater, corrupting his flesh and blood like a fire, and brings him into anguish, woe, and death: as man then experienced, and through the lustful eating of the earthly fruit of death, lost his heavenly body and his Divine image.

Thus, the poisonous eating had to be anointed and healed again through the eating of Divine Flesh; the fire quenched with water, the darkness driven out with light, and death killed with life.

Therefore, the Word of God enters into the death of man with the promise of new life, like a hidden little flame of fire, and grows in the Covenant through the fiery Law and sacrifice, until the time is fulfilled. Then it is conceived by the Holy Spirit, and the name **Jesus** <note>Böhme often interprets the name "Jesus" as the sweet, redeeming power of God that "soothes" the fiery wrath.</note> reveals itself in Christ out of Mary in twofold flesh and blood; He lets the old mortal self die on the † <note>The symbol of the cross.</note>, and gives to the soul the Divine heavenly [substance] with water and blood: to the young children in the **Ens** <term>Ens: A Latin-derived term Böhme uses to describe the essential, spiritual "being" or "substance" of a thing.</term> of life through water-baptism for their hunger; to the elders in the opened desire for grace as food and drink; so that a New Body may grow within the Old in the new Divine Will.

## Title-Figure XVIII. Of Divine Revelation in 177 Theosophical Questions.

The revelation of GOD in the **Trinity** <note>original: "Dreyzahl"</note> is considered in the creation of the angels, of this world with its creatures, and of man as the divine image. This includes the creation of the three hierarchies or angelic thrones: **Michael**, **Uriel**, and **Lucifer**. It was Lucifer who corrupted his throne, so that it had to be fashioned into the heavens, stars, and elements in its out-forming <note>Böhme suggests the material world was created as a containment for the fallen Lucifer's realm.</note>. In his place, **ADAM** is created from all three principles with a twofold body—Paradisiacal and earthly—yet glorified; he stands on earth and is simultaneously in Paradise. He **imagines** <note>In this context, "imagining" means to focus the creative power of the will.</note> intensely toward the starry, fiery nature of the spirit of this world, and this spirit in turn toward him. Thus, he is ignited by the **astral influence** <note>original: "Astro"</note> through his reason, becoming coarse and dark in desire. This darkens his crown—the divine likeness in the light—with the **source-quality** <note>original: "Paradeis-Qual." Böhme uses "Qual" to mean both "torment" and "the quality or source of a being."</note> of Paradise like a cloud. He thus falls into the **magia** <note>The supernatural or formative power of the will.</note> of this outer bodily nature, dies to the kingdom of heaven, and is manifested in a coarse animal body with all these affects and properties.

But the name **JESUS** forms itself with the character of the Trinity of the Cross <note>†</note> in his soul for rebirth. He manifests himself in the prototype under Moses with fiery letters of the Law, and in his assumed humanity on the Day of Pentecost in fiery tongues and flames of love of the Holy Spirit. Through this Spirit, He will also at the end dissolve the world through fire from all bodily coarseness, separating the good from the evil—the lambs from the goats—and manifesting man again in His kingdom in power, light, glory, and eternal peace. This is the subject of this little book, which was indeed begun by the author, but not completed.

## Title-Figure XXI. Regarding the Epistles.

In the title page of the **Epistles** <note>The "Send-Briefe," or theosophical letters of Jacob Böhme.</note>, there is a dove with an olive branch on the right, and on the left the city of **Alexandria** or **Leiden**, with the dove that carries a letter tied below it, as is known from history. Thus there are two doves; in the middle above, between these two, is the **Holy Spirit** in the form of a dove with 24 Pentecostal flames or fiery tongues of the spirit-letters, and the Gospel of peace. Thus there are three doves, signifying the **threefold spirit**: 1. of **GOD**, 2. of **Nature**, and 3. of **Art**.
